## Entergy Arkansas encourages customers to prepare homes, communities for fall safety


Simple steps, including inspecting heating equipment and reporting streetlight outages, can help keep families safe as days grow shorter and temperatures drop


Posted:


Nov 12, 2026


|


Posted:


[Lamor Williams](https://www.entergy.com/author/lamor-williams-2-2-2-2-2-2-2-2-2-2-2-2-2-2-2-2-2-3)

LITTLE ROCK, Ark. — As temperatures begin to cool and daylight hours grow shorter, Entergy Arkansas is encouraging customers to take a few simple steps to prepare their homes and communities for the fall season.


From making sure heating equipment is ready for colder weather to reporting streetlights that are not working, a little preparation can go a long way toward protecting families and improving community safety.


**Get your home heating system ready** Before turning on the furnace for the season, have heating equipment inspected and cleaned by a qualified professional. The National Fire Protection Association recommends annual maintenance of furnaces, fireplaces and chimneys to help ensure they operate safely.


Customers should also keep these heating safety tips in mind:


- Never use an oven to heat your home.
- Turn portable space heaters off when leaving a room or going to bed.
- Keep children at least three feet away from fireplaces, space heaters and other heating equipment.
- Test smoke alarms at least once a month.


Entergy Arkansas also offers programs designed to help customers improve their homes’ energy efficiency, including energy audits and HVAC tune-ups. Customers can learn more about available energy-efficiency resources at[entergy.com](https://www.entergyarkansas.com/energyefficiency) .


**Help keep streets and neighborhoods safe** The end of daylight-saving time brings earlier sunsets and longer periods of darkness, making properly functioning streetlights especially important for visibility and community safety.


Although Entergy Arkansas lighting teams routinely patrol and inspect streetlights the company owns or maintains, the company encourages customers to report any streetlights they encounter that are not working.


There are three convenient ways to report a streetlight outage:


- **Entergy mobile app:** This is the recommended reporting method. After logging in, select the outage map feature. The app can use your device’s GPS to pinpoint your location or allow you to manually enter an address. You can then select the specific streetlight maintained by Entergy. Make sure location services are enabled if using GPS.
- **Online:** Visit entergy.com and select the “Report an outage” option.
- **By phone:** Call 1-800-9OUTAGE to report a streetlight issue.


Not all streetlights are owned or maintained by Entergy. Some are the responsibility of another utility, local municipality or state agency. Customers can use the streetlight icon displayed on Entergy’s outage map to help determine whether a particular light is maintained by the company.


**Don’t overlook other seasonal safety reminders**


Fall is also a good time to prepare for seasonal changes in routines and weather. Health officials recommend annual influenza vaccinations, and customers should remain alert while driving as shorter days can mean reduced visibility and increased risks on the road.


Changing the clocks is also a convenient reminder to check smoke alarm and carbon monoxide detector batteries throughout the home.


Taking these precautions now can help families enjoy the season while preparing for the colder months ahead.
